findings.rationale: The finding misreads UNSTRING COUNT IN: GnuCOBOL 3.1.2 stores the number of characters examined for the field (the whole piece before the delimiter), not the number that fit into PIC X(8). The returned tree's own build stage prints BAD ACCOUNT for the panel's input, and the graded corpus already contained the case (generated_01 line 11). Kept the reference; added three over-width account lines to postings_account_identifiers so the corpus states the case explicitly, and marked the rule in the reference as checked against the binary.

findings.rationale: FUNCTION INTEGER is the greatest integer not greater than its argument (INTEGER-PART truncates). GnuCOBOL 3.1.2 prints WHOLE -2 for ADJ -1.20 on the panel's own input, and the graded postings_rounding_modes fixture already holds ADJ -12.345 (expected WHOLE -13) and ADJ -0.50 (expected WHOLE -1), both produced by the verifier's COBOL build and passed by the reference on the platform. Kept ROUND_FLOOR and marked it as checked against the binary.

findings.rationale: Core: the verifier must not tell the candidate which case it is running. Per-case names were rev1's answer to fixed paths; the repaired runner keeps a fresh random scratch tree per run (so the rev1 fixed-names port still fails) but uses the same neutral names for every case, so argv, cwd and environment carry no label.
